# vk 0.9.0 — owned allocator device retention

Development release, 2026-10-31. Cargo package **`vkrust 0.9.0+1.4.365`**,
Rust library/import name **`vk`**, Git tag **`v0.9.0`**, MIT licensed.
The `+1.4.365` suffix identifies the unchanged pinned Vulkan header snapshot;
it is not a Vulkan 1.4 driver requirement.

[Developer guide](https://dev.realm.software/vk) ·
[Rust API reference](https://docs.rs/vkrust/latest/vk/) ·
[Realm](https://realm.software/)

## API and migration

This is a minor API release: `Allocator` gains an internal `DeviceRetention`
reference-or-`Arc<Device>` device owner, exported as a public enum in
`vk::mem`. Three new constructors produce `Allocator<'static>`:

- `Allocator::new_retained(device: Arc<Device>, properties, block_size)`
- `Allocator::new_retained_with_granularity(...)` with explicit granularity
- `Allocator::new_retained_from_physical_device(physical_device, ...)`

A retained allocator holds its own `Arc<Device>` clone, so it outlives the
construction scope and can travel to a dedicated cleanup/retirement thread.
`SynchronizedAllocator::new_owned` adopts a retained allocator directly,
without the borrowed-lifetime adoption contract. Internal `BindOperation`
and `MapOperation` storage retains the device through the same enum.

The borrowed `new`, `new_with_granularity` and `new_from_physical_device`
constructors and every existing `Allocator`, `SynchronizedAllocator` and
free-function contract are unchanged. Use Cargo requirement
`version = "0.9"` with feature `allocator` for memory APIs.

## Evidence and limits

The release checkpoint passed 3,439 workspace tests/doctests on the private
tree, including the scoped retention proof
`retained_allocator_outlives_scope_and_finishes_on_worker_thread`, which
exercises scope-independent lifetime, synchronized worker-thread allocation
and final teardown on a dedicated thread against the native ledger. Strict
Clippy and rustfmt pass. Release CI reruns the configured tests,
package/consumer checks and pinned-header oracles on this release's exact
public snapshot.

No new sanitizer, VMA donor or native-hardware qualification was run for this
delta; the v0.8.0 scoped evidence carries forward unchanged for the borrowed
paths. Retained ownership is exercised by the native-ledger tests and by OA's
consumer migration, not yet by the released hardware profiles. The allocator
remains Experimental; all v0.8.0 qualification limits continue to apply —
see the [qualification report](../qualification.md). No fastest, full parity
or production readiness claim follows from this release.
